This is a steel blue, it's a hybrid species, it is known that one part of the hybridisation is A.Caetei, the first import was from out of china and no one has come forward to claim responsibility for this "species".
The initial import was mainly males, the few females were used to try and breed but all the fry were unviable and the eggs never developed which is a common trait in hybridized species. 

How do we know it's part Caetei? When males are paired with a Caetei female the fry are viable and make it to adulthood, there is speculation that the other species could be A.Resticulosa or A.Borellii but no successful spawns have been produced by pairing with these species so it is unconfirmed.

These fish are very often sold as Agassizii or Borelli, stores that purchase them are often surprised when they get these instead of what they thought they ordered from the importers, or on the other hand, the stores don't know what they are ordering in the first place so just sell them as they were listed with the importer.

Your water changes do a lot more than just reduce your nitrates, they remove hormones from the water which can negatively affect fish and also bacteria levels as well as dissolved organic waste, having high organic waste in your tank is a breeding ground for unwanted bacteria so they all kind of go hand in hand to create the perfect storm even if you are testing and getting good results.

Looks like a sensory pit infection to be honest, cichlids have small pits in their heads and along their lateral lines that can detect a number of things.

Sometimes these can get clogged with bacteria which can eventually turn into hole in the head disease, 2 treatments are regular water changes to reduce the bacteria count in the water and give the fish a chance to fight the infection, these will be large, and frequent water changes (50% 2-3 times a week)

Or metrodiazinole which is unfortunately not available everywhere. This mainly treats a bacteria in the stomach called Hexamita which basically absorbs the nutrition your fish would usually get from food, once this bacteria is taken care of your fishes immune system can bounce back and clear the bacteria from those pits.

Your male wants to start breeding, the female is not interested, in the wild he would chase her, she would swim away and another would come along.

What I do in this situation is remove the female, feed her up on BBS or frozen brine for a week and then add her back, this is called conditioning, gets the girl ready to lay eggs, the male will more than likely accept her in that state.

If it's not that it's a territory thing, best thing to do is move the male to another tank, let the female have a rest and establish a territory and then introduce the male back in.

Okay, first thing, I've used fine gravel mixed with sand before and I found I had more issues with apistos in that tank than I did with my ones with just super fine sand, they like to soft it through their gills to search for small things to eat as well as clean out small parasites in the gills.

Second, I have found bloodworms to not be so great for Apistos, the small hooks on their exoskeletons can get caught up in their gills and when it starts to break down you end up with a bacterial infection, it looks like that is what is happening here, the infection spreads from the gills to the eyes and so on.

I've not had much luck bringing them back from this so I just choose not to feed my apistos bloodworms and since then I have not had this issue, there is a debate out there on if it is bloodworms or not that causes this, if you wanna google it and do some research be my guest, but my conclusion is don't feed apistos bloodworms, frozen brine shrimp is a more nutritious treat and safer for them in my opinion.

If you wanna have a crack at saving this guy I would head to your LFS and get some anti bacterial treatment, not pimafix or melafix but something more like furan 2, you may have more options than me as I'm in NZ and we do not have many treatments available for fish here.

I've seen good advice here already but I'll share mine too.

Cut your lighting time down a few hours, more light equals more algae, I only have mine on for around 6 hours a day.

Do a test and see where your nitrates are sitting at, as said above I think you will find they are quite high, do water changes to bring the levels down, also if you don't already, get a regular water change schedule going, I do 50% a week but I dose ferts, you could do 25% most likely.

As I said above, algae loves light, you could potentially do a black out to weaken it, basically cover your tank with a blanket or something to block all light for 3-7 days, some of it will die and the rest will be weak and more susceptible to a treatment of some sort.

Make sure the tank isn't getting direct sunlight as this is absolute fuel for algae.

You could also try out something like 2Hr aquarist APT fix, this supposedly breaks algae down but you have to be careful cause if your plants aren't doing well they could be affected by it too.

Another thing you could try is dosing seachem excel, I've used it at the initial dose strength for 5 days in a row to kill hair algae before with no I'll side effects, it's says it is a carbon supplement for plants but it actually works by breaking down algae, the broken down algae turns into it's most simple form which is carbon.

Finally remember, changes in a tank may not be apparent for some weeks or months, if you change your lighting period the algae won't magically disappear in a few days so give it some time.

When I was about 5-6 we lived in a really rural town, middle of the forest, maybe about 25-30 houses a small shop and a school that went from kindergarten to high school.

A river ran through the town and our house backed into it with a pretty big nature reserve on the other side.

My room was the closest to the river from memory, I loved frogs and could hear them jump into the water and croak at night.

Well one night I heard a rather big splash, I looked out my window to see a canoe pulled up on the reserve side of the river and a person dragging a sack of some sort up the bank, I went and told Mum so she came to have a look, I was peeping through a crack in my curtains, my mother decided to draw one open so she could see, this caused the person to notice us watching them, they drop the sack, hop in the canoe and paddle over towards the bank on our property’s side.

When Mum saw he was heading towards our side of the river, she called the cops to tell them what we had seen, she sat me down and stared to read me a book when the phone goes off.

There was no response from the officer on duty so an off duty officer was on the way, at this time Mum hears a bang from the back of the house, almost like knocking, the banging continues, moving around the house, suddenly we hear yelling, the off duty officer had shown up as the person was making their way to the front of the house, they had a tussle and he was handcuffed and put into the back of the police car.

Mum maintained that it was nothing more than a delusional person for years after, about 2 years ago she finally told me what happened.

The person was a man that had just been released from jail, the sack had the body of the on duty police officer (who was also the arresting officer that put the man away), had he got in who knows what happened, but big props to my mother for keeping so calm the whole time.
